To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Kiss2 is widely expressed in the brain of the half-smoothed tongue sole (C. semilaevis) and that Kiss2 decapeptides directly regulate hypothalamic reproduction-related gene expression, including the kiss2 gene itself.

Kiss2 receptor and Kiss2 peptide are expressed in the brain of the half-smoothed tongue sole and that Kiss2 peptide can directly modulate the expression of reproduction-related genes in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonad axis.

Kiss2 receptor is widely expressed in tissues of the tongue sole, and that Kiss2 peptide can regulate the hypothalamic expression of several genes involved in the control of the reproductive axis of this fish species.

the molecular characterization of kiss2r and the in vitro effects of kiss2 on reproduction-related genes in the hypothalamuses of the half-smooth tongued sole.
the role of Kisspeptin/Kisspeptin receptor system in the regulation of reproduction-related genes in teleost fish.

the identification and molecular characterization of kiss2r in tongue sole, and the effects of Kisspeptin-2 (Kiss2) decapeptide on the expression of reproduction-related genes in the hypothalamuses of half-smooth tonguesole.

Kiss2 is involved in the control of GnRH neuronal activity and reproduction-related gene expression at the level of the hypothalamus in the half-smouth tongue sole.
kiss2r mRNA expression in the tongue sole hypothalamus is regulated by Kiss2, and that Kiss2 is a key regulator of reproduction-related gene transcription.

Kiss2 may be involved in the regulation of GnIH and Kiss2 production in tongue sole.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Kiss2 may play a role in regulating reproduction-related gene expression at the level of the hypothalamus in tongue sole.
Kiss2 may act as a negative regulator of reproduction in tongue sole.
